brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Conceptually fresh metaphor mapping musical chords to color triads, giving the tool a distinctive identity beyond generic palette pickers
Clean dark-mode chrome with disciplined typography hierarchy in the right rail makes harmony types scannable and calm
Color swatches sized boldly enough to feel like instrument pads, reinforcing the play-to-generate metaphor
dominant_weaknesses: Generated palette is crude primary RGB — saturated red/green/blue clash and undermine the promise of musical 'harmony' producing harmonious color
Piano keyboard is awkwardly cropped at the bottom-left, breaking spatial balance and feeling like an afterthought rather than the core instrument
Empty fourth slot (Seventh) and vast dead canvas center create visual imbalance; the stage lacks rhythm or grouping logic
fix_priorities: Replace literal RGB output with perceptually-tuned palettes (HSL/LCH harmonies) so chord-to-color actually produces aesthetic results
Reposition and full-width the piano as a grounded instrument bar; tie key presses visually to swatches with motion/glow
Resolve empty-state for Seventh slot and tighten vertical composition so swatches, keys, and rail share a coherent grid
Introduce subtle animation linking note press → swatch pulse to make the chord metaphor felt, not just labeled
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept outpaces visceral execution, and behavioral feedback between piano and swatches is missing entirely.
rationale.intent_fit: The metaphor is legible and promising, but the harmonies neither sound nor look 'locked' — execution falls short of the poetic brief.
